### Summary

This appendix is the index that the chapters cite for an environment variable: one row per variable, with the
function that reads it at the pin, its default, its effect and the chapters that use it. @sec-ch12 owns the
treatment: the parsing rules in @sec-ch12-environment, the launch variables in @sec-ch12-layout and the switch
combinations in @sec-ch12-matrix. Variables that only snapy's tests read are in @sec-ch12-test-environment and are
not repeated here.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Index of every environment variable snapy reads or sets at the pin, for the chapters to cite.

**Data.** 18 variables in four groups: 2 numerics switches, 11 launch and process-group variables, 3 UCX defaults,
2 build variables.

**Placement.** `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT`: the first call of its accessor; `SNAP_ANOMALY`: every read of a deck's
`dynamics` rows. Launch: each construction and each deck read of layout options. The Gloo interface: process-group
construction.

**Activation.** Both switches are off unless set; `SNAP_ANOMALY` overrides the deck key `dynamics/anomaly`. The
launch variables default to one process on the CPU.

**Guarantee / limits.** `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is read once per process, `SNAP_ANOMALY` at every deck read;
nothing checks that ranks agree.

**Evidence.** The ctest arms of @tbl-appd-tests; full treatment in @sec-ch12-environment.
:::

Two numerics switches are read from the environment at the pin. `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` makes the hydro of a
spherical-polar grid read plain means instead of $r^2$-weighted cell averages in the reconstruction and the $x_1$
pressure source, while the scalar keeps its $r^3/3$ table (@sec-ch12-centroid). It is an environment variable and
not a deck key because every block of a process must make the same choice, or the two sides of an $x_1$ seam stop
agreeing; the accessor's own comment says so ({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}).
`SNAP_ANOMALY` is the environment override of the deck key `dynamics/anomaly`, which stores the density and energy
rows of the state as anomalies about a static FP64 reference; the options schema marks the row with the variable
({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}}), the generator writes the read into the deck reader
({{< code tools/gen_options.py env >}}), and the reader runs it after the deck value every time hydro options are
read from a deck ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).

The other numerics choices a reader may look for here are deck keys, listed in @tbl-appd-keys and in @sec-appi:
the lateral face-flux covariance (`dynamics/flux-covariance`, on by default), the radial velocity mean correction
(`dynamics/x1-mass-covariance`, off by default) and the fourth-order cell-consistent reference
(`dynamics/conversion-order: 4`). The corrected potential-energy face work has no switch at all: it follows from
`gravity-work: face`, the one accepted value, with nonzero `grav1` on a grid that has an $x_1$ measure
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::radial_exact_work >}}).

The scope is `src/`, `python/` and `setup.py` at the pin. Variables read by kintera, pyharp, commux, PyTorch, Gloo
or UCX themselves are not listed, except the one Gloo variable snapy reads on their behalf,
`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`.

### Derivation

None: the switches select schemes whose derivations are in @sec-ch12-centroid, @sec-ch03 and @sec-ch12; the launch
variables select no numerics.

### Numerical method

`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is decided once per process, in five steps fixed by its accessor
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}):

1. *Read.* `get_env` returns the variable's value when it is set, the empty string included, and the accessor's
   default `"0"` only when it is absent ({{< code src/layout/layout.hpp get_env >}}).
2. *Normalise.* The value is lower-cased; it is not trimmed, so `false ` with a trailing space is a value of its own.
3. *Decide.* The switch is off when the value is empty, `0`, `false`, `off` or `no`. Every other value is on.
4. *Cache.* The result is kept in a function-local `static`, so the first call fixes it for every block of the
   process, and a later change of the environment has no effect.
5. *Act.* Five sites read the cached value. The coordinate's $x_1$ row faces take the plain-mean branch on a
   spherical-polar grid ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::x1_row_faces >}}); the spherical-polar
   forward builds the $x_1$ pressure-source stencils when face pressures are defined
   ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}); the hydro forward converts the
   primitives of a spherical-polar block to plain means before the reconstruction
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}); the hydro setup reads it for the `nghost`
   requirement below ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}); and the balance of a rest column refuses
   any geometry but Cartesian ({{< code src/hydro/balance_column.cpp balance_column >}}). On a Cartesian or
   gnomonic-equiangle grid the first three sites do nothing, and the scalar's $r^3/3$ table is not touched on any
   grid.

The switch shares one requirement with `dynamics/conversion-order: 4`: both read scan pressures three cells away,
so with nonzero `grav1` the block needs `nghost` of at least 3, checked at setup
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).

`SNAP_ANOMALY` takes a different path. The options schema marks the `dynamics/anomaly` row with
`env: SNAP_ANOMALY` ({{< code src/options/hydro.yaml >}}), and the generator writes the read into the deck reader
({{< code tools/gen_options.py env >}}): after the deck value, if the variable is set, `1`, `on`, `true` or `yes`
turns the key on, an empty value, `0`, `off`, `false` or `no` turns it off, and any other value is refused. The
read runs every time hydro options are read from a deck
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), so nothing caches it, and the Python
options have no such key (the row is marked `python: false`). With the key on, setup requires the `ideal-moist`
equation of state and a Cartesian grid and installs the FP64 reference store
({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}); a restart of a multi-block run needs the file's `hydro_ref`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_restart.cpp >}}).

The launch variables are read each time layout options are constructed
({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::LayoutOptionsImpl >}}). The `BACKEND` default comes from
`default_backend` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp default_backend >}}): `ucx` in a build with UCX, except on macOS,
else `gloo`. The deck reader reads `BACKEND` and `DEVICE` a second time, through the same generated mechanism as
`SNAP_ANOMALY`: the schema's `backend` and `device` rows carry `env:` entries, so a set `BACKEND` overrides
whatever the deck says, and the device is `DEVICE` or `cpu` when it is unset ({{< code src/options/layout.yaml >}},
{{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). The deck's `distribute/backend` key is accepted
and ignored, and there is no deck key for the device. A Gloo process group reads
`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` once, when it is constructed, and binds its device to that interface instead of resolving the
host ({{< code src/layout/process_group.cpp ProcessGroupContext::_init_gloo >}}). The three communication defaults
are written, not read, by `set_default_env` ({{< code src/layout/process_group_ucx.cpp set_default_env >}}), only
when the variable is unset and only in a build with UCX, as the UCX process group starts
({{< code src/layout/process_group_ucx.cpp ProcessGroupContext::_init_ucx >}}); they are listed because they change
the process environment that commux sees.

### Code

**How to set a switch.** It is an environment variable of the process that runs snapy, set before it starts;
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` has no YAML key, and `SNAP_ANOMALY=1` turns `dynamics/anomaly` on without one. For example, the Straka deck in `build/bin` of a build at the pin
([Install and run](#sec-preface-install)):

```sh
SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT=1 ./straka.release straka_single.yaml
```

The deck is Cartesian, so the switch changes no number of that run; it only adds the `nghost` requirement of
refusal 1 below, which the deck's `nghost: 3` meets. A run with several processes needs a common rendezvous port,
which `torchrun` sets from `--master-port`:
`torchrun --no-python --nproc-per-node=2 --master-port=29573 ./straka.release straka_proc2.yaml`.

**What is refused, and why.** For `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` nothing in the parse refuses a value: an unrecognised
value turns the switch on (step 3 of the Numerical method above). The parse refuses one value of `SNAP_ANOMALY`,
and setup refuses five combinations:

1. *`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` (or `dynamics/conversion-order: 4`) with nonzero `grav1` and `nghost` below 3*: the
   resolution flag reads scan pressures three cells away, so both sides of an $x_1$ seam agree only with three
   ghost cells ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
2. *`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` with a rest column whose geometry is not `cartesian`*: `balance_column` does no
   $r^2$-to-plain-mean conversion, so a spherical-polar column's rest state is left to the solver's own reference
   ({{< code src/hydro/balance_column.cpp balance_column >}}).
3. *`SNAP_ANOMALY` set to anything but `1`, `on`, `true`, `yes`, the empty value, `0`, `off`, `false` or `no`*:
   the generated reader stops with `SNAP_ANOMALY must be 0 or 1` ({{< code tools/gen_options.py env >}}).
4. *`dynamics/anomaly` on (by deck or by `SNAP_ANOMALY`) with an equation of state other than `ideal-moist`, or on
   a grid other than Cartesian*: the anomaly storage is implemented for that one EOS and one grid
   ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}).
5. *An unset `MASTER_PORT` with either world size above 1*: the processes could not meet on one store
   ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::LayoutOptionsImpl >}}).
6. *`GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME` naming an interface the host does not have*: the Gloo device is created for that interface
   and the process group fails to start on every rank with `Unable to find address for: <name>`
   ({{< code src/layout/process_group.cpp ProcessGroupContext::_init_gloo >}}); `test_gloo_invalid_interface` in
   @tbl-appd-tests expects exactly that failure on both ranks.

**The code, mapped to the five steps of the Numerical method above**
({{< code src/coord/x1_centroid.cpp x1_centroid_exact_enabled >}}):

```cpp
bool x1_centroid_exact_enabled() {
  static const bool on = [] {                                    // step 4: once per process
    auto v = get_env("SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT", "0");             // step 1: default "0" only if unset
    std::transform(v.begin(), v.end(), v.begin(),
                   [](unsigned char c) { return std::tolower(c); });   // step 2: lower-case, no trim
    return !(v.empty() || v == "0" || v == "false" || v == "off" || v == "no");  // step 3
  }();
  return on;                                                     // step 5: read at five sites
}
```

### Tests

The table covers the ctest entries that set an environment variable of this appendix; the tests of the deck keys
of @tbl-appd-keys belong to the sections that explain those keys (@sec-ch12-flux-covariance,
@sec-ch12-mass-covariance, @sec-ch04-conv4) and are not repeated here. The registrations set the switches and the
backend per entry ({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}), as the entry's own environment or inside a wrapper script
the entry runs; the three Python entries set `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` in their own source, for a child process or
for the script itself. Two further groups set a variable of @tbl-appd-layout only to launch the case they test, and
the table lists them as groups: eight entries whose wrapper script or test source starts its ranks with
`BACKEND=gloo`, and eleven Python entries that set `DEVICE` and `DEVICE_ID` to the device under test. Each row is
one variable or one group; the test names are the registered ctest names, without the build-type suffix. The seam arms pass only on gtest's own line
`[  PASSED  ] 1 test.`, so a skipped or empty arm fails its entry.

: Ctest entries that set an environment variable of this appendix, at the pin. {#tbl-appd-tests}

The registered names and their assertions are in @sec-appc. No check script of this report covers this appendix.
Twelve entries of @tbl-appd-tests were run at the pin for it[^appd-run]: eleven passed, and
`test_gloo_invalid_interface` failed for a reason that is not the interface check. Its binary compiles
its one test only with `NETCDFOUTPUT` ({{< code tests/test_output_barrier.cpp >}}), so in a build without NetCDF
both ranks run zero tests and exit 0, and the wrapper stops with `expected two interface errors; exit=0,
matches=0`. In a build with NetCDF (`-DNETCDF=ON -DPNETCDF=ON`, same tree, same host) the entry passes, with
`test_output_barrier` itself. The wrapper entry `test_sedimentation_cubed_seam_gloo` and the two `SNAP_ANOMALY`
entries, `test_anomaly_storage_python` and `test_options_table`, passed in the same build[^appd-run], as did the three
Python `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` entries. Of the two launch groups, `test_exchange_decomp` and the two CPU entries of
the `DEVICE` group passed in the same build and the nine CUDA entries skipped; the seven other `BACKEND=gloo`
entries read back NetCDF output and failed there because none was written, and all seven passed in the build with
NetCDF[^appd-run]. The CUDA and UCX-on-GPU arms were not run.

[^appd-run]: `ctest -j 1` on the entries by name, in a Release build at the pin configured with `cmake -DCUDA=OFF
    -DNETCDF=OFF -DPNETCDF=OFF -DUCX=ON`, kintera 2.6.13, pyharp 2.7.17, torch 2.10.0+cu128, Linux x86-64, the
    multi-rank entries as two or three `torchrun` ranks on one host. Passed: `test_x1_seam_split_x1_centroid`,
    `test_x1_seam_split_nghost_check_x1_centroid`, `test_x1_seam_split_mp_x1_centroid`,
    `test_deck_x1_wiring_x1_centroid`, `test_stretched_x1_ref_x1_centroid`, `test_balance_column_x1_centroid`,
    `test_face_floor_x1_centroid`, `test_x1_centroid_rest_python`, `test_diffusion_cubed_sphere_mp`,
    `test_conservation_budget_mp`, `test_parentless_cloud_nb1_mp_gloo`, `test_exchange_ucx`, in a second run
    `test_sedimentation_cubed_seam_gloo`, `test_anomaly_storage_python`, `test_options_table`, and in a third run
    `test_radial_order_x1_centroid_python`, `test_stencil_cache_small_block_python`, and in two further runs
    `test_exchange_decomp`, `test_fp32_science_python`, `test_seam_rotation_cache_python` (the other nine `DEVICE` entries
    skipped, code 125). Failed: `test_gloo_invalid_interface`, as described, and the seven NetCDF-writing `BACKEND=gloo`
    entries for want of NetCDF output. In the build with NetCDF (`-DNETCDF=ON -DPNETCDF=ON`, same tree, same host), the
    seven passed: `test_restart_multiblock`, `test_restart_dt_change`, `test_restart_output_schedule`,
    `test_restart_key_collision`, `test_restart_inplace_reorder`, `test_netcdf_axis_attrs`, `test_restart_resume_schedule`,
    5 s to 29 s each. One run each, one host.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A switch that differs between ranks makes shared faces two-valued, and no code compares the ranks' values.
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` changed after the first call has no effect in that process; `SNAP_ANOMALY` is read again
at every deck read, so two decks read in one process can disagree.
:::

- `distribute/backend` in YAML is accepted and ignored; only `BACKEND` selects the backend.
- `SNAP_ANOMALY` reaches a deck read only; options built in code or from Python carry no override.
- `LOCAL_RANK` has two defaults: 0 in the C++ layout options, the rank modulo the GPU count in `init_dist`.
- An unset `NC_HOME` adds the literal path `None/lib` to the package build's library path.
- The scope is `src/`, `python/` and `setup.py` at the pin; environment variables read by kintera, pyharp, commux,
  PyTorch, Gloo or UCX themselves are not listed, apart from `GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME`, which snapy reads itself.
- The CUDA and UCX arms of @tbl-appd-tests register only in a build with that option; the evidence above is a CPU
  build without CUDA, so those arms are not run here.
